title: Note On/Off per electrode
statement: Each of the 12 electrode inputs E0–E11 (MPR121 ELE0–ELE11) shall send one MIDI Note On, on the configured channel (default 1) with the configured fixed velocity (default 100, range 1–127), when a touch is detected. It shall send a Note Off for the same note when the touch is released.
evidence: I: PASS. The chain terminal → series resistor → module electrode is 1:1 (interface_check `pcb.A2.pin2..13`, `pcb.J2.*`). T: NOT RUN.

title: Note Off integrity
statement: The Note Off for a pad shall carry the note number sent in its Note On, even if the scale or octave changed in between. All sounding notes shall be released before a recalibration.
evidence: Host tests PASS (`reports/firmware/T-043/checks.log`, 268 host tests passed). Hardware test NOT RUN.

title: Second sensor (24 pads)
statement: The firmware shall support a second MPR121 at I2C address 0x5B (`NUM_SENSORS = 2`), mapping its electrodes to pads 12–23. This is a breadboard-only option; the PCB carries one module (ADR-007 D-3).
evidence: A: latency PASS at 400 kHz (12.07 ms ≤ 15 ms, jitter 8.07 ms), using the worst-case run-based burst plan (budgets.out §b). T: NOT RUN.

title: Polyphonic aftertouch
statement: While a pad is touched, the device shall send Polyphonic Key Pressure (0xAn) with a value 0–127. The value shall map linearly from delta = baseline − filtered, clamped to [12, 120]. It shall be evaluated every 15 ms and sent only when it changes by at least 2.
evidence: Host tests PASS (`reports/firmware/T-043/checks.log`, 268 host tests passed). Aftertouch messages are sent after all Note On/Off of the same loop (ADR-010). Hardware NOT RUN.

title: Six scales
statement: The device shall provide 6 scales, selected cyclically: Drum Rack (36–47, octave ignored, the power-on default), major pentatonic, minor pentatonic, major, natural minor and chromatic (root 48). Notes shall be clamped to 0–127.
evidence: A: notes 24–99 with 12 pads and 24–127 with 24 pads, never clamped (T-009 budgets §d). Host tests PASS (T-040 `test_scales.py`).

title: Octave potentiometer
statement: The octave potentiometer shall shift melodic scales by −2..+2 octaves using 5 ADC zones with a hysteresis of 0.7 zone. It shall have no effect on Drum Rack, and shall be enabled by default on the PCB build.
evidence: A: the ADC offset of 30 mV (SOURCE S-01 §4.3) is 6.5 % of the 0.462 V hysteresis (CALCULATION). Host tests PASS (`test_pot.py`). Hardware NOT RUN.

title: Button short press
statement: A short press of the button (released within 800 ms, sampled every 10 ms) shall select the next scale, and the LED shall blink N times for scale N.
evidence: Host tests PASS (`reports/firmware/T-043/checks.log`, 268 host tests passed). Hardware NOT RUN.

title: Button long press recalibration
statement: A press of more than 800 ms shall release all notes and recalibrate all sensors; the LED then blinks 3 times.
evidence: Host tests PASS (`reports/firmware/T-043/checks.log`, 268 host tests passed). Recalibration blocks for 16.8–22.1 ms per sensor at 400 kHz (CALCULATION); this is user-requested and allowed by REQ-016. Hardware NOT RUN.

title: Sensor-absent behaviour
statement: If no MPR121 answers, the device shall send no MIDI, blink the LED at 5 Hz and retry every 2 s.

title: Status LED
statement: The LED shall give 2 slow blinks at start when a sensor is found, and shall be lit while any pad is touched. On Pico W and Pico 2 W the LED is driven through the CYW43 (WL_GPIO0).

title: USB MIDI class compliance
statement: The device shall enumerate as a USB MIDI 1.0 class device (MIDIStreaming, bulk endpoints). It shall work without vendor drivers on Windows 10, Windows 11 and macOS 12 or later.

title: Device name
statement: The USB product string and the MIDI port name shall be "FrutaMIDI".
evidence: I: `DEVICE_NAME = "FrutaMIDI"` is passed to `setProductDescriptor` and `setStringDescriptor`. T: NOT RUN.

title: MIDI message set
statement: The device shall send only Note On (0x9n, CIN 0x9), Note Off (0x8n, velocity 0, CIN 0x8) and Polyphonic Key Pressure (0xAn, CIN 0xA), on one channel n = MIDI_CHANNEL − 1. Incoming MIDI shall be read and discarded.
evidence: `fm_midi.h` constants match S-14 Table 4-1.

title: Touch-to-MIDI latency
statement: Device latency from touch to the USB-MIDI packet being available to the host shall be ≤ 15 ms worst case, for electrode capacitance ≤ 100 pF, with mitigation M1 (one burst read per sensor per aftertouch pass).
evidence: A: PASS. 1 sensor 10.59 ms, 2 sensors 12.07 ms at 400 kHz (ADR-008). The worst aftertouch pass is the run-based plan from fm_mpr121.h: 42 bus bytes in 8 transactions (mask 0x925); every loop also reads `touched()` (2 B). Design limit C ≤ 210 pF (CALCULATION, budgets.out §b, revision 3). T: NOT RUN (plan item P-2). Flagged for user review (ADR-007).

title: Latency jitter
statement: Latency jitter (worst minus best) shall be ≤ 10 ms for electrode capacitance ≤ 100 pF.
evidence: A: PASS. 6.59 ms (1 sensor) and 8.07 ms (2 sensors) at 400 kHz (CALCULATION). T: NOT RUN.

title: No blocking during play
statement: During play, no firmware action other than a user-requested recalibration shall block touch processing for more than 10 ms.
evidence: I: the only `delay()` in firmware is `delay(10)` in `midiBegin()` (setup, FrutaMIDI.ino:111). LED feedback is non-blocking (`fm_blink.h`). A: worst loop 1.59 ms at 400 kHz. Firmware T-041..T-043 is complete (`reports/firmware/T-043/checks.log`, 268 host tests passed).

title: USB bus power only
statement: The device shall be powered only from USB VBUS through the Pico's micro-USB connector. No other power input shall exist.
evidence: Pico pins 39 and 40 are unconnected (`pcb.A1.no_other_nets`).

title: VBUS range
statement: The device shall operate with VBUS from 4.40 V to 5.50 V at its connector.
evidence: A: VSYS 3.95–5.25 V, inside the SOURCE S-01 range of 1.8–5.5 V: PASS. However, the 4.40 V low-power-port minimum is below the Pico's recommended VBUS of 5 V ± 10 % (4.50 V; S-01 §2.3): budgets check A3b FAIL. The diode drop is an ASSUMPTION. T: NOT RUN.

title: VBUS current
statement: VBUS current shall be ≤ 100 mA (the declared bMaxPower, S-11) for every supported Pico board.
evidence: A: worst case 55.6 / 70.6 / 60.6 / 75.6 mA for Pico / Pico W / Pico 2 / Pico 2 W. Lower bounds are SOURCE (S-01 Table 3, S-16 Table 2); RP2040 pull-ups 50–80 kΩ are SOURCE S-17. The upper bounds are ASSUMPTIONs. T: NOT RUN (plan item P-3).

title: 3V3 rail load
statement: The external load on the Pico 3V3(OUT) shall be ≤ 300 mA with at least 50 % margin.
evidence: 10.15 mA worst case with 2 sensors and PCB pull-ups: 96.6 % margin.

title: MPR121 supply voltage
statement: The MPR121 VDD, fed from the Pico 3V3 through the module LDO, shall be within 2.0–3.6 V.
evidence: 3.10–3.40 V (CALCULATION; dropout and rail tolerance are ASSUMPTIONs).

title: Touchable voltage (SELV)
statement: Every user-touchable conductor shall be at ≤ 3.6 V relative to GND and shall be supplied only from the USB SELV source.
evidence: Electrodes are charged from MPR121 VDD ≤ 3.6 V (S-04), and REQ-017 holds.

title: Electrode ESD robustness
statement: Each user-touched electrode terminal shall survive ±4 kV contact discharge without permanent damage. The ±4 kV target is an ASSUMPTION, following IEC 61000-4-2 level 2 (the standard was not read).
evidence: A: the pin current is 1.10 A < 1.33 A at ±4 kV with 3.3 kΩ (R1–R12) (`reports/electronics/analysis.md`, my CALCULATION agrees). But no datasheet-confirmed pulse or voltage rating of at least 3.64 kV exists for the MFR-12 3k3, so the resistor may flash over (ADR-012, T-054). At 8 kV: PARTIAL, risk R-006. Change candidate CR-001 is Vishay MBB 0207. T: NOT RUN [PHYSICAL].

title: I2C hand-wire fault current
statement: A misplaced SDA or SCL hand wire (including one on a supply hole S1/S2/S6/S7) shall not drive an RP2040 pad beyond its IO current limits.
evidence: I: 220 Ω series resistors are present between the Pico pads and the bus: pad 31 SDA_PICO → R16 → SDA, pad 32 SCL_PICO → R15 → SCL (interface_check `fw.pcb.PIN_SDA/SCL_vs_pcb`). A: fault current 15.5 mA per line at 3.4 V, 30.9 mA for both lines, ≤ IIOVDD_MAX 50 mA (SOURCE S-17 Table 625). Low-level margins: Pico→MPR121 0.138 V, MPR121→Pico 0.235 V (budgets B5/B6, CALCULATION). Statement reworded after ADR-009 D-9: a wire on a supply hole is still physically possible, but it is now current-limited.

title: Both module revisions
statement: One PCB shall accept both Adafruit 1982 revisions. JP1 bridges ORIG (+3V3 → S1 = VIN) or QT (+3V3 → S7 = VCC). The SDA/SCL wires from J1 go to S5/S6 (original) or S3/S4 (STEMMA QT).
evidence: I: PASS. JP1 selector S1/+3V3/S7 with silkscreen legend 'ORIG = no white connectors' and 'QT = 2 white connectors' (`pcb.JP1_legend`). J1 1 = SCL, 2 = SDA. hardware/README.md table (JP1, SDA, SCL) = ORIG/S5/S6 and QT/S3/S4, which matches the Eagle-derived S-row (`doc.hw_readme.jp1_and_wires.*`). T: NOT RUN.

title: I2C rise time (PCB)
statement: The PCB-build I2C bus shall meet the rise time for its clock: ≤ 300 ns at 400 kHz (≤ 1000 ns at 100 kHz), with the module at 0x5A.
evidence: A: PASS. R13/R14 4.7 kΩ: t_r 156 ns at 60 pF, C_b limit 115.2 pF (systems, with RPU 80 kΩ from S-17); electronics gives 103 ns at 38 pF. The 220 Ω series resistors add 2.2 ns (ASSUMPTION of 10 pF pad capacitance). IO levels with 220 Ω: B5–B8 PASS, minimum margin 0.138 V (S-17 Table 625, S-04 Table 5). T: NOT RUN (plan item P-4).

title: Single-sided PCB
statement: The PCB shall be single-sided: copper on B.Cu only, through-hole parts only, no vias, no copper pour, and no wire bridges apart from the 2 I2C configuration wires and the JP1 solder bridge.
evidence: pcb_rules_check: all segments on B.Cu; 0 vias, 0 zones, 0 SMD pads.

title: Board outline
statement: The board outline shall be 100 × 70 mm.
evidence: Outline 100.000 × 70.000 mm. Board label 'FrutaMIDI v1.1' (`pcb.label_v1.1` PASS).

title: Home-etch rules
statement: Home-etch rules: signal tracks ≥ 1.0 mm (≥ 0.8 mm for short stubs), power tracks ≥ 1.2 mm, clearance ≥ 0.6 mm (DRC hard minimum 0.5 mm), annular ring ≥ 0.4 mm, drills ≥ 0.8 mm.
evidence: pcb_rules_check `SUMMARY: 14 checks, 14 PASS, 0 FAIL` on the current PCB (R15/R16 included); minimum annular ring 0.40 mm. Clearance relies on the electronics DRC (`reports/electronics/evidence/T-055/`), which systems did not re-run.

title: Screw-terminal map
statement: The PCB shall provide 14 screw terminals at 5.08 mm pitch: GND, E0..E11, GND. Terminal k (k = 2..13) shall reach MPR121 electrode k − 2 through its series resistor.
evidence: interface_check J2.T1..T14 and A2.pin2..13.

title: Pin map consistency
statement: The firmware PCB pin map (I2C1 SDA GP26 / SCL GP27, button GP22, pot GP28/ADC2) shall match the PCB nets. The breadboard map (I2C0 GP4/GP5, button GP15, pot GP26) shall match README.md.
evidence: interface_check: 0 pin mismatches.

title: Core BOM cost
statement: The core BOM (assembled board, excluding tools, consumables and USB cable) shall cost ≤ 30 EUR.
evidence: 20.42–30.40 EUR (CALCULATION, now including R15/R16). Nearly all prices are ASSUMPTIONs; the upper bound exceeds the target by 0.40 EUR. Quoted prices from one supplier would close this.

title: Firmware build matrix
statement: The firmware shall build without errors for Pico, Pico W, Pico 2 and Pico 2 W, each for the breadboard and PCB variants (FQBN `rp2040:rp2040:<board>:usbstack=tinyusb`, plus `-DFRUTAMIDI_PCB` for PCB), and for `arduino:avr:leonardo` (optional).
evidence: `reports/firmware/T-041/build/*.log`: 9 of 9 logs contain "Sketch uses …". A clean compile is not a hardware validation.

title: Browser sampler
statement: The browser sampler `docs/index.html` shall work in Chrome and Edge (Web MIDI) on Windows and macOS. It shall map its 12 pads to notes 36–47 by default, treat Note On with velocity 0 as Note Off, send unmapped notes to the synthesiser, apply aftertouch (0xA0) to the filter, and offer a keyboard fallback and dropped-file samples.
evidence: Automated browser tests with a stubbed Web MIDI PASS (T-020, T-021 handoffs). A real browser, a real device and audible output are NOT RUN.

title: English language
statement: All project files, code, comments, reports, generated PCB text, fabrication file names and user-visible strings shall be in English.
evidence: I: 0 Portuguese-word matches in firmware (`.ino`, `fm_*.h`), gen_*.py, docs/index.html, README.md, hardware/README.md and docs/manual/MANUAL.md. Silkscreen is English (SCALE, OCTAVE, ORIG, QT, legend, 'copper: bottom side'); fabrication file names are English; no broken relative links (`doc.links.*` PASS).

title: User and assembly manual
statement: The user and assembly manual shall match the current PCB. It shall cover both module revisions, the JP1 selector and data wires, flashing, first start, a valid pre-power continuity checklist and troubleshooting.
evidence: I: hardware/README.md (assembly) matches the current PCB: JP1 and two wires, R15/R16 220 Ω, JP1 legend, a continuity test that accounts for the 3.3 kΩ resistors, English silkscreen names, valid links (interface_check documentation `17 checks, 17 PASS, 0 FAIL`). README.md documents the breadboard 4.7 kΩ pull-ups. docs/manual/MANUAL.md (user manual) refers to JP1 and covers BOOTSEL/UF2 and troubleshooting. The inspection covered consistency with the design, not readability.

title: Sensing range (physical)
statement: [PHYSICAL] Touch detection shall work on objects from a bare pad (about 20 pF) to large fruit or a glass of water (up to about 500 pF, ASSUMPTION), with leads of 20–50 cm, after recalibration.
evidence: A: the MPR121 can charge up to about 1203 pF (CALCULATION). Latency targets hold up to 210 pF at 400 kHz. AUTOCONFIG limits USL/TL/LSL = 200/180/130 at design VDD 3.2 V and SCTS = 0 (0x7C D7) are now SOURCE (ADR-010/011, MPR121 datasheet S-006 in management/SOURCES.md). T: NOT RUN.

title: False triggers and crosstalk (physical)
statement: [PHYSICAL] There shall be no false Note On in 10 min idle with all 12 electrodes connected to objects, and no crosstalk when touching a neighbouring electrode.

title: JP1 cannot short 3V3
statement: No position of the JP1 3V3 selector (ORIG, QT, open) shall connect +3V3 to GND.
evidence: S1 and S7 are never GND in either revision (`pcb.JP1_no_gnd_reachable`).

title: JP1 wrong-position tolerance
statement: A wrong JP1 position (ORIG on a STEMMA QT module, or QT on an original module), or both sides bridged, shall not apply a voltage outside the MPR121 absolute maximum ratings (inputs ≤ VDD + 0.3 V, S-04 Table 3), and shall not short +3V3 through a module output.
evidence: A: still FAIL as stated. The ORIG bridge on a QT module puts +3V3 on ADDR, and the QT bridge on an original module puts it on IRQ, both above VDD + 0.3 V on an unpowered module. Both sides bridged on an original module ties +3V3 to the IRQ open drain. Mitigation per ADR-009 D-10: silkscreen legend present (`pcb.JP1_legend` PASS), manual warning, and the firmware 'sensor not found' LED pattern. Residual risk R-007 accepted by the manager.

title: I2C rise time (breadboard, with pull-ups)
statement: The breadboard-build I2C bus, with the two 4.7 kΩ pull-ups required by ADR-009 D-11, shall meet the rise time for 400 kHz.
evidence: A: PASS. t_r 156 ns at 60 pF with 4.7 kΩ (CALCULATION). Without them, 452 ns: FAIL above 39.8 pF. I: README.md lists the two 4.7 kΩ pull-ups in its BOM and wiring table. T: NOT RUN (plan item P-4).
